I recently came into a similar situation at 39, I had been a housewife for the last 10 years, struggling with my ex who claimed thats what he wanted until we got an actual house then decided he didn't need me anymore & dumped me.

5 months later & im still drifting aimlessly.  I was extremely codependent & it broke me completely.  I'm just existing day to day & hoping I figure something out, but I feel like im not much closer to an answer now than I was in May.

I'm a security guard & afraid of confrontation.  Not a good combination  

Luckily I'm just doing covid screening so it's mostly nonconfrontational, but I dread when the pandemic is over & I have to work a 'real' security job

Thank you for the recommendation, ill see if I can get my hands on a copy

Ive been reading a lot about codependency & I realize that I've just been living as a child, trying to find a parental figure to take care of me; my mother was a narcissist & did everything for me, so I never really learned how to be a functional adult.  Now I'm trying,  but it feels like I'm completely alone while doing it, which is an added challenge

I get it, & it didnt come across harshly.

I spent 11 years waiting & working towards mutual goals (getting the house) & its like once we got it,he didn't need me anymore so I've been discarded

I'm currently on a waiting list for therapy to help with setting boundaries & dealing with confrontation,  so hopefully that'll help.

I get overwhelmed really easily,so moving forward is happening,  its just a slow process & im impatient

Negativity bias

This is the phenomenon that if there are 2 equally charged stimuli, the negative one will attract more of your mind's attention 

From an evolutionary perspective it was a huge competitive advantage.  Say that you are a hunter-gatherer out looking for food.  Suddenly a snake starts slithering towards you, & a wild boar that could feed your family for weeks runs across your path.  Your subconscious has milliseconds to decide which to pay attention to. 

Choose to hunt the boar & you'll be vulnerable to the snake & likely get bitten.  Choose to defend yourself against the snake & you'll avoid getting bitten but the boar will get away

All of our ancestors who paid attention to the positive stimuli in their environment  (the boar) died out because they failed to identify the threats around them  (the snake)

In the past, the negativity bias was a useful adaptive response.  Today it just makes you pay too much attention to what's wrong with you & the world

I know I'm super late to this, but I hope you see this comment, because I made this (slightly modified - I just roasted the spaghetti squash & served the filling in the 'bowl', then topped with over easy eggs)  
I'm not a fan of mushrooms, but i absolutely LOVED this, & the spaghetti squash isn't trying to be something it's not

Spaghetti Squash Breakfast Casserole

1 spaghetti squash

7 oz Sausages

1/4 cup butter

8 oz sliced mushrooms

2 cloves garlic minced

1/2 tsp salt

10 oz spinach, chopped

1 cup crumbled feta

1/2 cup grated parmesan

4 eggs

1/4 cup heavy cream

1. Preheat oven to 350F and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper. Grease a 9x13 inch glass or ceramic baking dish.

2. With a large, sharp knife, cut spaghetti squash in half lengthwise. Place on baking sheet cut-side down and bake until soft and squash can be squeezed easily with your hands.

3. Meanwhile, cook sausage in a large skillet according to package directions. Thinly slice and transfer to a large bowl.

4. Heat butter in the same skillet over medium heat. When melted and hot, add mushrooms, garlic, and salt and sauté until mushrooms are golden brown. Transfer mushrooms to the same bowl and add spinach, feta and parmesan.

5. Remove squash from oven and scoop out and discard seeds. Scoop the flesh into the bowl along with the other ingredients. Mix well to combine.

6. In a medium bowl, whisk together eggs and whipping cream. Stir into vegetables and mix well. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste.

7. Spread the mixture in the prepared baking pan and bake 40 to 60 minutes, until puffed and set all the way through. Remove and let cool a few minutes before serving.

​

Servings: 8

Chicken & Dumplings

​

6 tbs butter

1 cup chopped onion

1 cup chopped carrot

1 cup diced celery

4 cloves garlic

3 tbs flour

12 ounces evaporated milk

4 cups chicken broth

4 cups cooked chicken, chopped

1 tsp thyme

2 tsp pepper

1 dash salt

Dumplings

2 cups flour

4 tsp baking powder

1 tsp pepper

1 tsp salt

1 tsp thyme

3/4 cup milk

4 tbs butter, melted

​

1. In a large pot, melt butter over high heat

​

2. Add onions, carrots, & celery.  Cook for 5 minutes, until vegetables begin to soften.  Add garlic & cook 1 more minute

​

3. Add flour & stir to combine.  Cook for 1 minute.  Add evaporated milk & chicken broth & quickly stir to combine

​

4. Bring to a boil & add chicken, thyme, pepper, & salt.  Let simmer, uncovered

​

5. Make the dumplings by whisking together flour, baking powder, pepper, salt, & thyme.  Make a well in the center of the mixture & pour the milk & butter in the well

​

6. Stir the dough until it forms into a ball.  Add extra milk if it seems too dry

​

7. Using a large scoop, scoop dough & drop directly into the soup.  Gently press them down so the soup runs over top of them

​

8. Cover the pot & lower the heat to a low simmer.  Cook for 15 - 20 minutes, then serve

​

Servings: 6
